No standard-setting registry for data-center baselines surfaced in the parent's research or in a fresh search of ordinances and guidance, which showed bespoke county-by-county language.

title: Warranty Desk Embedded in Maintenance Software
one_liner: A white-label, success-fee warranty desk sold through mid-tier maintenance-tracking and MRO software vendors. The removal event, the PO and the repair invoice meet inside a system the operator already uses, and the software vendor earns a revenue share.
customer: The channel buyer is the partnerships or customer-success head at a mid-tier maintenance-tracking or MRO software vendor with 50-400 operator customers. The payer is the operator on that software: a regional airline, Part 135 or cargo-feeder fleet, or helicopter operator. The vendor pays nothing. It receives 30% of our fee and gets a renewal and differentiation story.
problem: Operators on these systems already hold structured removal, install, hours and cycles data, plus POs and receiving records. That is the data-access problem the parent idea could not solve. Still, warranty stays unclaimed, because the missing pieces are things software does not do. Someone has to read negotiated PDF terms, file on each shop's own template, and chase the shop for 60-90 days. Vendors cannot staff claims specialists. Operators' thin materials teams cannot absorb the work. The claim is decided at the removal moment, when a technician pulls a unit at 3 AM and nobody sees the terms. Only the maintenance software sees that event.
solution: The vendor gives a read-only export or API for removals, installs, POs and receiving. We load each shop's warranty terms from the operator's contracts and invoice PDFs. When a technician posts a removal against a serialized component, we return a lookup card in seconds, inside the vendor's UI or by email or Slack in the first version. The card shows who repaired the unit and when, the remaining window in days, hours or cycles, the evidence checklist, and a pre-drafted claim. Our claims specialists then file, chase and post the credit memo back into the system as a warranty record. A monthly sweep catches misses, late turn times, no-fault-found fees and open cores. Operators sign a contingency agreement. The vendor contract is non-exclusive and revenue-share only.
why_now: LLM extraction of warranty fine print and invoice PDFs means one specialist can now run claims for dozens of operators. Software vendors are also under pressure to prove value in the renewals of small and mid-size operators. Ramco advertises warranty-recovery savings, which shows the outcome is being marketed. Nobody sells the outcome as a service to the other vendors.
revenue_model: Operators pay 20% of cash and credits recovered, with a 12-month tail. The vendor gets 30% of our fee, about 6 points of recoveries, and owns the relationship. From year 2, vendors can bundle a Warranty Desk line item at $1-2k/month per operator, with us as wholesale fulfillment at about $600/month plus the success fee. Aggregated vendor-level claim data is a later product.
non_obvious_insight: Maintenance software has an adoption problem, not a feature problem. Warranty fields and modules sit empty because filling them takes human work: reading PDFs and chasing vendors. A managed service that makes the module produce cash is worth more to a vendor than building the feature. The vendor also supplies what our own sales cycle lacks: structured removal data, a warm introduction, and a trigger at the exact moment the claim is won or lost. Vendors will not build claim-chasing themselves. Terms are negotiated PDFs, and staffing claims desks is not a software margin.
first_30_days: Approach 8 mid-tier software vendors' partnership heads with a one-page offer: we make a slice of your customers' warranty tracking pay, with no cost to you and 30% of our fee. Ask each for 2-3 design-partner operators. Work as a concierge service, with no integration yet. The operator exports removals, POs and receiving from the software's standard CSV export, we match against invoice PDFs, and we deliver a ranked claim list with the vendor's customer-success manager on the call. Build the removal lookup as a simple web form or email responder. Sign a revenue-share MOU with the first vendor and aim for the first credit memo by day 30-45. Hire a retired materials coordinator for shop quirks. Success is 2 operators with live removal-time lookups by month 3.

The offer differs from an ERP module because it is done-for-you and paid only on results. It avoids the data-access problem by using the vendor's structured data. It also avoids cold sales to small operators, since the vendor's existing customer base and success team provide distribution.

title: Nonrenewal Desk for Colorado Independent Agencies
one_liner: An agent-side triage-and-evidence service that starts when a Front Range nonrenewal or score-disclosure notice lands, and charges most of its fee only when the policy is saved.
customer: Owner-principals of independent insurance agencies in Boulder, Jefferson, Larimer, El Paso and Douglas counties. Each has 150+ wildland-urban-interface homeowner policies, is appointed with 6 or more carriers so it can re-market, and has received several nonrenewals or surcharge notices since January 2026. Colorado only. California is dropped until AB 75 is confirmed enacted.
problem: When a nonrenewal or score disclosure arrives, the agent has about 10 days to get an acknowledgement and about 30 days to a decision (HB25-1182). The agent has no verified evidence, and the free homeowner kits (FireRisk.ai, Defensible Space Score) only produce letters. A corrected score may not move the premium, because insurers can meet the law with a manual mitigation discount and do not have to accept third-party imagery. The agent loses the commission and the bundled auto and umbrella policies, roughly $600 a year or more per WUI household.
solution: The agent forwards the notice PDF and gets three things within 48 hours. (1) A Lot Ledger: dated 15-50 cm imagery and public lidar canopy and clearance measurements set against each feature the insurer disclosed. Each feature is marked contradicted, confirmed or unknowable. (2) A Credit Map: for each carrier the agency is appointed with, which filed mitigation credits or underwriting-exception paths the evidence supports, so the pack asks for the premium or retention outcome and not just a score change. (3) A carrier-formatted pack timed to the 10 and 30 day clocks, plus a re-marketing shortlist when the appeal is weak. The desk declines to file when the evidence does not contradict the score. That keeps the concession ledger clean and makes carriers trust the packs. After trust is built, the same imagery layer is run across the agency's whole WUI book to flag likely errors before renewal.
why_now: HB25-1182 has been in force since July 1, 2026, so disclosures, appeals and the 10/30-day clocks are now real for every Colorado WUI policy. Independent agents are the ones absorbing the nonrenewals. Public regional aerial flights, USGS-style lidar and cheap commercial archives mean the first appeals need no imagery licence. I did not verify that insurer appeal desks are unprepared, so the plan does not rely on it; the trigger is the notice itself.
revenue_model: $249 per month per agency, including 5 triage runs and a book scan of up to 300 WUI policies. Extra packs are $149 each. A flat $300 success fee applies per policy retained or re-marketed within 90 days of a pack. There is no percentage of premium, to avoid producer-compensation and rebating problems. At 20 agencies, that is about $60k in subscriptions plus roughly $90k in success fees, around $150k ARR, with gross margin above 70% once imagery is bought per filed case only.
non_obvious_insight: The product is a decision about what will actually change the outcome: fix the input, harden the house, or re-market it. It is not a rebuttal letter. Honest triage is the moat, because a desk that refuses weak cases gets a higher concession rate, and a concession ledger keyed by carrier, vendor, input error and evidence type becomes something carriers cannot get elsewhere. Carrier-side vendors like Zesty, Nearmap and Cotality cannot sell against their own customers' scores. That is counter-positioning.
first_30_days: Recruit 6 Front Range agencies through a Colorado independent-agent association or by direct outreach to principals. Run concierge delivery by hand with an analyst using public imagery, lidar and QGIS, with no licensing. Give the first 5 files per agency free and charge $99 from file 6. Aim for 40 real notices and 20 filed appeals with outcomes tracked. Send agencies a private weekly concession scoreboard as the sales asset.

title: Verified Pay Receipts for Truck Driver Hiring
one_liner: Drivers upload settlement stubs and AI turns them into the true, receipts-backed pay per mile and per hour away from home for every carrier, sold as a hiring credential and as income proof for lenders.
customer: Honest mid-size carriers (50 to 1,000 trucks) that pay $6k to $15k to hire each driver and can't prove their pay claims are real. Secondary buyers are mortgage and auto lenders (bank-statement and non-QM brokers) who serve drivers.
problem: Recruiter ads say 'up to 75 cents a mile, $100k+' but realized pay is often 20 to 35% lower after unpaid or practical-versus-paid miles, unpaid detention, chargebacks and deductions. Driver turnover at big truckload carriers runs near 90%, and job ads are so discredited that honest carriers can't stand out. Drivers whose pay is structured as tax-free 'per diem' also see a low W-2 and get denied mortgages after 20 years of work. Estimates say the English-proficiency and non-domiciled CDL crackdowns will pull 214,000 to 437,000 drivers (5 to 12% of CDL holders) from the supply over 2 to 3 years, so carriers are competing harder for domestic drivers.
solution: A mobile app where drivers photograph settlement stubs and pay statements. AI extracts paid miles, deadhead, detention, deductions, per diem and time away from home, and computes effective take-home per hour on the road, not just per mile. Public carrier pages show verified figures such as '312 verified drivers, median $0.61 per paid mile, $17.40 per hour away'. Carriers that look good pay for a 'Verified Pay' badge and applicant funnel. A second product builds an income-verification packet from stubs and deposit statements for lenders. Fraud controls include stub-format checks, duplicate detection and consistency with driver-reported miles.
why_now: Shrinking driver supply from the 2025 to 2026 English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement (proposed codification rule published Aug 10, 2026) and the Feb 2026 non-domiciled CDL restrictions means cost-per-hire is rising. Vision-model OCR of messy pay stubs is now cheap and accurate. Truth-in-leasing rules already require itemized settlements, so the raw material exists.
revenue_model: Carrier subscriptions of $500 to $3,000 a month for the verified page, analytics and applicant funnel. Lender referral fees of $300 to $1,000 per funded mortgage or truck loan. Free for drivers, which keeps the data supply growing.
non_obvious_insight: Drivers don't compare carriers by ads, they ask in the truck-stop lot 'what do you actually clear?' The only artifact they trust is a pay stub. The honest carriers are the ones locked out of trust, so they are the natural paying customer. The true unit of pay is dollars per hour away from home, because 14-hour clocks, detention and unpaid waiting eat the mileage math. And per-diem income structures are a hidden mortgage trap that a stub-based income packet can fix.
first_30_days: Post in trucker Facebook groups, Reddit and TikTok: 'Upload your stub, see your real rate vs. what your carrier advertised.' Aim for 500 stubs in 30 days. Publish a 'State of Real Pay' report ranking 20 named carriers and pitch it to trade press (Overdrive, CDLLife, FreightWaves). Sell 'Verified Pay' badges to the 5 mid-size fleets whose numbers look best, and sign one bank-statement mortgage broker for lender leads.

competition_context:
Competitor check: GAP. Closest players: TruckersReport (carrier reviews and salary survey), Best Fleets to Drive For (CarriersEdge), Tenstreet (Driver Pulse, IntelliApp, Hiring Center), Drive My Way. White space: Web search was unavailable (the session's 200-search budget was used up), so this rests on about 25 direct page fetches plus prior knowledge. Confidence is moderate to low. A reviewer should re-run searches for 'verified driver pay', 'settlement stub scanner' and 'trucker mortgage per diem' before committing.

I found no product that does all of this: (1) collect settlement stubs, (2) verify them with fraud checks, and (3) publish per-carrier, receipts-backed effective pay, including dollars per hour away from home. The closest, TruckersReport, has an unverified self-reported salary survey run by a site paid by carriers' recruiting budgets. Best Fleets to Drive For is survey-based. Tenstreet and Drive My Way own recruiting flow but show no pay-verification product.

Specific unserved gaps:
- A trust-backed pay number that uses stubs as proof, computed as dollars per hour on the road rather than per mile.
- Lease-purchase and owner-operator drivers, whose settlements are itemized and who are the most exposed to deceptive ads.
- A stub-based income packet that handles per-diem structures for non-QM and bank-statement lenders. Truv and Argyle verify through payroll connections and are not built for per-diem trucker income.

Weak points that could still sink it:

5. Per-funded-loan referral fees to a non-lender may run into RESPA Section 8, so this needs counsel. Lenders will also likely re-verify borrower-supplied stubs, which limits the lender product's value. This is from prior knowledge and not verified.

title: Nonrenewal Cure: Rebutting Insurer Cancellations
one_liner: Nonrenewal notices often cite fixable issues like roof condition, tree overhang or debris. Sell homeowners a fast diagnosis, repair and evidence packet to get re-underwritten instead of dumped on a FAIR plan.
customer: Homeowners in CA, FL, TX, CO, UT and NM who have received a nonrenewal notice, plus independent brokers who lose those clients.
problem: Nonrenewals are at records and homeowners have 30-75 days to react. Carriers are structurally conflicted about helping, and the FAIR plan is pricey with thin cover. Homeowners can't decode the reason code, can't tell which items are cheap to fix, and can't produce the evidence a carrier re-inspection accepts.
solution: Upload the notice. The service decodes the stated reason using state disclosure rules, dispatches vetted local contractors for the fix (patch, trim, vent screens), and produces a time-stamped photo and invoice packet. It files for reinspection or appeal, and gives the broker a clean file to re-market the risk. For wildfire-score cases it documents mitigation credits available under state rules.
why_now: Record nonrenewals, California passed three claims and nonrenewal bills on 2026-09-03, and insurance now rivals mortgage payments. Carriers rely more on aerial-imagery flags that homeowners rarely see or contest.
revenue_model: $149 diagnostic, $250-$500 evidence packet, 10-15% contractor referral fee, and broker referral fees on re-placed policies.
non_obvious_insight: Many cancellations are cheap to cure, but the homeowner has no language, time or evidence, and the carrier won't help. A homeowner who has just been rescued becomes a lifetime referral source for brokers.
first_30_days: Post in local nonrenewal threads and neighborhood groups, and partner with three independent brokers. Handle 20 cases by hand, track how many carriers reinstate, and use the win rate to set pricing.

title: Fixed-Price Guaranteed Clearance of Unknown Lead Lines
one_liner: Take the whole unknown-lines problem at a fixed price per line with an acceptance guarantee, and make money by routing each line to the cheapest method that will satisfy the state (records mining, meter-swap photos, paid photos, probe, pothole).
customer: Utilities with 5,000-100,000 unknown lines and a deadline, and the state programs or state revolving fund offices that want a known cost to fund. Wedge: a mid-size utility that has run out of staff or budget for engineering time-and-materials billing and can issue phased task orders under the small-purchase limit ($25-50k each). Later customer: a state that buys 'unknown clearance' for all its small systems.
problem: The industry sells effort: engineering firms bill hours, probe vendors sell hardware or crew days, modelers sell licenses, and portals sell software seats. No one sells the outcome the utility actually needs, which is 'this unknown line is now known and the state accepted it.' Utilities carry the acceptance risk, the routing decision and the cost overrun. The cost ladder is steep and poorly used: a records lookup can cost a few dollars, a photo $6-40, a scheduled visit around $120, a probe crew several hundred, a pothole about $900 or more, and a replacement thousands. Most utilities either dig too much or wait years.
solution: An 'unknowns clearing' contractor with a router at its core. Tier 0: predictive scores and assessor data on year built and neighborhood (bought from BlueConduit, VODA or open sources). Tier 1: vision-model mining of the utility's own tap cards, plumbing permits and old work orders, handwritten records that are now readable by multimodal models at $1-3 per line. Tier 2: three-photo protocol captured during meter swaps, inspections, water-heater changes and owner self-ID through a leadCAST- or Esri-style intake. Tier 3: scheduled visit by a panel plumber. Tier 4: probe or acoustic crew subcontracted from Electro Scan- or Echologics-type providers. Tier 5: pothole. Each line goes to the cheapest tier that the state accepts for that housing and meter archetype. The company quotes a blended fixed price per unknown (about $60-70) for a portfolio, guarantees acceptance (a rejected reclassification is redone free and the fee refunded), and holds a reserve for rejections. Evidence is exported in the state format and feeds the utility's Esri layer. First product for a scrappy team: an 800-1,000-line pilot with a spreadsheet-and-vision-model router and part-time inspectors.
why_now: Multimodal models can read old tap cards and permits and classify pipe photos, which collapses the cost of tiers 1 and 2 in 2025-2026. Inventory rules and the replacement clock (federal details still in flux, several state statutes independent of them, verify) make 'unknown' a budget line. Infrastructure-law SRF money is under spend-down pressure and funders prefer priced outcomes. Utilities are short of engineers, so buying an outcome is more attractive than buying hours. The photo, probe and prediction vendors now exist as suppliers to a router, which they did not five years ago.
revenue_model: Fixed price of about $60-70 per unknown, contracted in phased task orders of 500-1,000 lines each. Target blended cost is $28-35 per line, a rejection reserve of about 8%, and gross margin of roughly 45-50% at scale. Working capital comes from an initial reserve of a few hundred thousand dollars, then from SRF draws on accepted lines, and eventually acceptance-risk reinsurance so a third party underwrites the guarantee. Upside comes from the router's data: measured accuracy and cost per method by housing archetype, which improves margin every contract and can be sold to states as a benchmark. Later, sell state-wide 'unknown clearance' bundles.
non_obvious_insight: There are two inversions. First, price the outcome, not the effort. Hourly engineering firms and hardware vendors cannot copy a fixed price per accepted line without cannibalizing their own revenue. Second, treat the competitors as suppliers. Every tier below the pothole is somebody else's product, and the profit is in the routing decision and the guarantee, not in owning a method. The bigger unlock is that most unknowns turn out to be non-lead, so the cheapest method that proves it is almost always far below the dig cost. That spread, multiplied across tens of millions of unknowns nationally (verify with public inventory totals), is the business.
first_30_days: Days 1-10: pick one state with a written acceptance path. Approach five utilities in it and ask for a sample of their tap cards and unknown list. Run the vision model on 200 cards and measure how many lines it resolves. Days 10-20: build the router as a spreadsheet: for each address, cost, expected accept rate and method by tier. Line up one probe subcontractor and 10 part-time inspectors. Days 20-30: quote the first utility a fixed $65 per line for 800 unknowns, with a rejection reserve of $40k and a right to redo any rejected line free, structured as two task orders under the small-purchase limit. Ask the state program to confirm the acceptance path in writing before signing.

title: Evac Cash: Payout When Ordered to Evacuate
one_liner: A few dollars a month buys a $500-$2,500 wire within hours of an official mandatory evacuation order for your address, covering hurricane, wildfire and burn-scar flood orders.
customer: Renters and lower-to-middle-income homeowners in evacuation zones: Gulf and Florida surge zones, Western wildfire-urban-interface neighborhoods, and LA burn-scar areas. Sold to individuals, through employers of hourly staff (hospitals, hotels, nursing homes, grocers), and through credit unions or municipal 'evac funds'.
problem: Evacuating costs $1,000-$3,000 (gas, hotel, lost shifts, pet boarding) and the money is needed before any claim exists. Cost is a common reason people stay, so the people most exposed are least able to leave. Civil-authority and additional-living-expense cover is slow, receipt-based, often conditional on nearby damage, and many renters lack it.
solution: A parametric contract whose trigger is a legal act. If your geocoded address sits inside a polygon under a mandatory evacuation order, or an NWS flash-flood emergency for a burn scar, the platform pays via FedNow/RTP or a push-to-card within hours. Zone data comes from county emergency-management systems (evacuation-zone platforms and state zone maps). Tiers are priced by zone frequency, with one payout per event per address and a simple app that alerts you and shows your zone. Underwritten via a licensed MGA and fronting carrier, first as employer group policies.
why_now: Address-level, machine-readable evacuation zones are now common. FedNow/RTP make hours-not-weeks payouts cheap. The LA fires of January 2025 made burn-scar exposure vivid, and NOAA CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks show a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Niño this winter, which means heavy rain on fresh burn scars and flash-flood/debris-flow evacuation orders. Parametric reinsurance capacity is plentiful and MGAs want small-ticket distribution.
revenue_model: Premium of roughly $3-$15 per month depending on how often each zone is ordered out (about 1.3-1.5x expected payout), or $1-$3 per employee per month on group plans. The company keeps an MGA commission of 15-25%, plus municipal, nonprofit and employer-funded policies for vulnerable residents. Later it can sell zone-frequency data to emergency managers.
non_obvious_insight: The best parametric trigger is a legal act, not a physical measurement. An evacuation order is binary, public, address-specific and timestamped, so basis risk nearly vanishes. Paying people to leave also changes behavior and saves lives, which makes employers and governments willing co-payers, so the product has two buyers instead of one.
first_30_days: Sign a parametric MGA and fronting carrier. Build the polygon match and instant-payout flow on public evacuation-zone data. Pilot a group policy for about 200 hourly workers at one Gulf hospital or hotel employer and one credit union serving a LA burn-scar community. Offer emergency-management agencies a free 'what zone am I in' tool for distribution. Goal: 500 covered addresses before peak rain season.
